name: Arches National Park
title: Holidays in Arches National Park
intro: More than 2,000 natural stone arches in the red desert just outside Moab, Utah, with short walks to some of the most famous rock shapes on earth. Here's what Arches National Park is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: North Window, a large sandstone arch in the red rock of Arches National Park
facts_note: The park charges an entry fee per vehicle, or buy an America the Beautiful annual pass if you're visiting several parks. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Spring and autumn are best: April, May, September and October bring warm days that are good for walking. June to August is very hot, so walk at sunrise or sunset and rest in the middle of the day. From April to October you usually need a timed entry reservation to drive in during the day, so book ahead. Winter is cold, quiet and often lovely, with no reservation needed.

things.name: Delicate Arch
things.blurb: Utah's most famous arch, at the end of a three-mile round walk over open slickrock. Go for sunset and bring plenty of water.

things.name: The Windows
things.blurb: A cluster of huge arches a short, easy walk from the car park, with Double Arch just across the road.

things.name: Balanced Rock
things.blurb: A giant boulder perched on a thin pillar, right beside the road with a short loop path around it.

things.name: Devils Garden and Landscape Arch
things.blurb: A flat-ish trail to one of the longest arches in the world, with scrambles beyond for older children.

things.name: Fiery Furnace
things.blurb: A maze of narrow fins and passages, best visited on a ranger-led walk. Book well ahead.

things.name: Moab
things.blurb: The lively town at the gate, with diners, ice cream, bike hire, rafting trips on the Colorado and jeep tours.

faqs.question: Is Arches National Park good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many arches are a short walk from the road, the park is compact, and Moab has plenty for families. Delicate Arch is a good first proper hike for school-age children.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Two or three nights in Moab covers Arches and a day in Canyonlands next door.

faqs.question: How do you get there?
faqs.answer: Fly to Salt Lake City and drive about four hours, or fly to Moab's small Canyonlands airport, which has flights from Denver. Grand Junction in Colorado is under two hours away.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Do you need a reservation for Arches?
faqs.answer: From April to October you've usually needed a timed entry ticket from Recreation.gov to drive in between about 7am and 4pm. Check the park website for this year's dates.
